newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end higher in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end higher in active trade.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended higher in active trading that was fueled, at least in part, by the government's decision late last week to exempt most actively traded shares from a new capital gains tax, traders said.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index closed 2.15 percent higher at 15,297.96 on an above-average trading volume of 2 billion pesos. Bogota's IBB gained 1.45 percent, meanwhile, closing at 979.74. Volume in Bogota was an active 4.7 billion pesos.

Gainers included brewer Bavaria SA -- the country's third most actively traded stock and part of the powerful Julio Maria Santo Domingo industrial group -- which closed up 5.15 percent in Bogota to end at 6,320 pesos per share.
Cementos Argos SA, the fourth most active last year, also closed sharply higher, gaining 6.34 percent in Bogota to end at 6,700 pesos per share.
"There was demand from Bogota and Medellin and vice-versa. People were asking for shares wherever they could get them," one broker said of the run on both Argos and Bavaria.
He attributed the buying spree to Bavaria's high liquidity and what he described as Argos' "excellent investment portfolio."
Other big winners included Bancoquia, the target of a takeover by Spain's Grupo Santander. The bank closed up a sharp 5.66 percent to end the day at 2,853 pesos per share.

Brokers attributed most of the day's gains to last Friday's announcement by Bogota stock exchange president Carlos Caballero to the effect that the government had decided to exempt Colombia's 41 most actively traded stocks from a new capital gains tax declared in January.
